question: Compare the magnetic field inside a long solenoid and inside a toroid. Why is the magnetic field outside an ideal solenoid weak, while outside an ideal toroid it is nearly zero? Give reason.

options.A: Inside a solenoid, $B=\dfrac{\mu_0NI}{2\pi r}$ and is circular; inside a toroid, $B=\mu_0nI$ and is uniform. The outside field is zero for both.
options.B: Inside both a solenoid and a toroid, the field is uniform and given by $B=\mu_0nI$; neither confines its field.
options.C: Inside a long solenoid, $B\approx\mu_0nI$ and is nearly uniform along the axis. Inside a toroid, $B=\dfrac{\mu_0NI}{2\pi r}$ and is along circular paths. The external solenoid field is weak because lines are mainly concentrated inside, whereas an ideal toroid has nearly zero outside field since an external Amperian loop encloses zero net current.
options.D: A solenoid has no field outside because it is an open toroid, whereas a toroid has a strong radial field outside.
